data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

extract_result.subject: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) Policy
extract_result.opi: Office of the Chief Information Officer, Digital Infrastructure Services Center

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for implementing the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Memorandum M-18-23, Shifting From Low-Value to High-Value Work across the USDA.
cross_references: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Memorandum M-18-23, Shifting From Low-Value to High-Value Work
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy

policy_statements.source_text: It addresses the establishment of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) through the Center of Excellence (CoE) within the USDA Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO).
policy_statements.target: establishment of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) through the Center of Excellence (CoE) within the USDA Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO)

policy_statements.source_text: RPA tools are software programs designed to interact with existing applications and automate routine rules-based tasks by mimicking user interactions.

RPA tools reduce the burden of repetitive, simple tasks on employees, and have the potential to save time and taxpayer dollars, improve accuracy and productivity, ensure standardization and consistency of service, and free Federal employees to focus on more meaningful and analytical work.
policy_statements.target: burden of repetitive, simple tasks on employees

policy_statements.source_text: This policy creates the basic framework for RPA at USDA.
policy_statements.target: basic framework for RPA at USDA

policy_statements.source_text: This policy may reference and mandate compliance with other directives.

Compliance with such policies must defer to, and be superseded by, any prevailing or more recent Acts of Congress, Executive Orders, Presidential Policy Directives (PPD), and OMB memoranda, circulars, and guidance.
This policy supports the OMB, The President’s Management Agenda (PMA), which focuses on the modernization of the Federal workforce.
cross_references: OMB, The President’s Management Agenda (PMA)

policy_statements.source_text: This policy applies to all USDA RPA capable processes and systems in USDA, and to Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, contractors, grantees, and others working for or on behalf of USDA.
policy_statements.target: all USDA RPA capable processes and systems in USDA, and to Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, contractors, grantees, and others working for or on behalf of USDA

policy_statements.source_text: All USDA RPA development systems must adopt the RPA CoE development model.
USDA RPA services must comply with all current Federal laws, USDA Information Technology (IT) security and risk management policies, and OCIO acquisition approval.
policy_statements.target: all current Federal laws, USDA Information Technology (IT) security and risk management policies, and OCIO acquisition approval

policy_statements.source_text: USDA RPA services must comply with all Federal and Departmental privacy requirements, regulations, and policies, which will be reviewed periodically to align with changing the IT landscape and incorporate process and policy improvements.
policy_statements.target: all Federal and Departmental privacy requirements, regulations, and policies

policy_statements.source_text: USDA RPA service acquisition vehicles must include Service Level Agreements (SLA) with clear, concise, and detailed language identifying the Service Provider responsibilities for accommodating Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA 2014), and reporting and privacy management requirements per OMB Memorandum M-21-02, Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Guidance on Federal Information Security and Privacy Management Requirements.
cross_references: Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA 2014)
OMB Memorandum M-21-02, Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Guidance on Federal Information Security and Privacy Management Requirements

policy_statements.source_text: USDA RPA services must comply with DR 3180-001, Information Technology Standards.
cross_references: DR 3180-001, Information Technology Standards

policy_statements.source_text: USDA RPA services must comply with the OCIO Information Security Center (ISC) Compliance and Policy Branch (CPB) standard operating procedure (SOP), CPB-SOP-004, USDA Seven-Step Risk Management Framework (RMF) Process Guide (USDA RMF).
cross_references: OCIO Information Security Center (ISC) Compliance and Policy Branch (CPB) standard operating procedure (SOP), CPB-SOP-004, USDA Seven-Step Risk Management Framework (RMF) Process Guide (USDA RMF)
policy_statements.target: OCIO Information Security Center (ISC) Compliance and Policy Branch (CPB) standard operating procedure (SOP), CPB-SOP-004, USDA Seven-Step Risk Management Framework (RMF) Process Guide (USDA RMF)

policy_statements.source_text: USDA RPA services must comply with DR 3540-003, Security Assessment and Authorization [A&A], and the CPB Guidance Memo, Fiscal Year (FY) 2020 Security Assessment and Authorization (A&A) Guidance.
cross_references: DR 3540-003, Security Assessment and Authorization [A&A]
CPB Guidance Memo, Fiscal Year (FY) 2020 Security Assessment and Authorization (A&A) Guidance

policy_statements.source_text: USDA RPA services, including applications and functions residing on local computers and Departmental, Mission Area, agency, and staff office infrastructure, must use mature agile methodology as well as development, security, and operations (DevSecOps) best practices per USDA RPA CoE strategy.
cross_references: USDA RPA CoE strategy
policy_statements.target: mature agile methodology as well as development, security, and operations (DevSecOps) best practices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA RPA CoE strategy further provides that Mission Area, agency, and staff office IT staff should become familiar with lean product management, agile development, continuous delivery, and automated infrastructure at the team and program level as part of any modernization plan.
cross_references: USDA RPA CoE strategy
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office IT staff

policy_statements.source_text: Additionally, non-IT staff supporting privacy, security, and procurement should receive training in the multiple core disciplines outlined above.
policy_statements.actor_name: non-IT staff supporting privacy, security, and procurement
policy_statements.target: training in the multiple core disciplines outlined above

policy_statements.source_text: Sustained progress in these staff training areas is foundational to the successful implementation of new automation (RPA) efforts.
USDA RPA Program Office governs both Centralized and Federated Center of Excellence (CoE) operational models.
policy_statements.target: both Centralized and Federated Center of Excellence (CoE) operational models

policy_statements.source_text: In the Centralized Model, the RPA CoE owns and manages the entire process for bot (a computer program that performs automatic repetitive tasks) intake, development, and production in coordination with the business area process owners.
policy_statements.target: entire process for bot (a computer program that performs automatic repetitive tasks) intake, development, and production

policy_statements.source_text: The Federated Model business area manages their intake, development, and production with RPA CoE touchpoints at strategic integrals.
All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must contact the CoE at SMORPA@usda.gov for all new RPA adoption efforts.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: for all new RPA adoption efforts

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must report all existing and new RPA solutions and services to the CoE , including Pilot Projects, Proof-of-Concept projects, training, and learning activities.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: all existing and new RPA solutions and services

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must develop RPA solutions using the Department’s approved automation software suite.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must acquire the Department approved RPA licenses and operating environments via the OCIO Digital Infrastructure Service Center (DISC).
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: Department approved RPA licenses and operating environments

policy_statements.source_text: All USDA RPA development projects must include the involvement of a Qualified Service Provider (QSP).
policy_statements.target: involvement of a Qualified Service Provider (QSP)

policy_statements.source_text: Whether using the Federated or Centralized CoE model, developers must meet the following QSP criteria to ensure quality products to the Department.
conditions: Whether using the Federated or Centralized CoE model

policy_statements.source_text: The following language must be part of any procurement for RPA Services:

The vendor or contractor must demonstrate that at least one member of the contract development team working directly on USDA automation, possesses an RPA Developer Advanced Certificate of Completion from the Department’s approved software vendor to be considered a QSP.
policy_statements.target: at least one member of the contract development team working directly on USDA automation

policy_statements.source_text: Note: Formal Federal Regulatory authority or industry standards have yet to establish a baseline for accreditation or competency.
The Certificate of Completion proves that the user has successfully passed the Department’s approved software vendor’s RPA Developer Exam.
It demonstrates that the graduate has been tested on the Department’s approved software vendor best practices and demonstrated their ability to develop a functional software robot.
The Certified Developer must be part of the development team.
Managers and supervisors from the developer’s employer do not satisfy this requirement.
policy_statements.actor_name: Managers and supervisors from the developer’s employer

policy_statements.source_text: Security

All new application development efforts will bring security to the application and infrastructure by incorporating modern software development best practices, such as continuous monitoring and accredited platforms.

All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must abide by DR 3640-001, Identity, Credential, and Access Management [ICAM], according to OMB, M-19-17, Enabling Mission Delivery through Improved Identity, Credential, and Access Management, to employ ICAM policies where applicable.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
cross_references: DR 3640-001, Identity, Credential, and Access Management [ICAM]
OMB, M-19-17, Enabling Mission Delivery through Improved Identity, Credential, and Access Management
policy_statements.target: DR 3640-001, Identity, Credential, and Access Management [ICAM]

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will comply with the security requirements of the DISC.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA will expand its continuous diagnostic capabilities for RPA solutions.
policy_statements.target: its continuous diagnostic capabilities for RPA solutions

policy_statements.source_text: Acquisition

All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must comply with DR 3130-009, Non-Major Information Technology (IT) Investments for non-major investments and DR 3130-010, United States Department of Agriculture Enterprise Information Technology Governance, and DR 3130-008, Definition of Major Information Technology Investments for major investments to ensure successful outcomes that align with business needs while meeting approved costs, schedule, and performance goals.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
cross_references: DR 3130-009, Non-Major Information Technology (IT) Investments
DR 3130-010, United States Department of Agriculture Enterprise Information Technology Governance
DR 3130-008, Definition of Major Information Technology Investments

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must employ high-quality IT cost estimation practices per DR 3130-012, Information Technology Cost Estimating.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
cross_references: DR 3130-012, Information Technology Cost Estimating

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must comply with IT capital planning and investment control (CPIC) practices per DR 3130-013, Information Technology Capital Planning and Investment Control, and embrace Technology Business Management (TBM) framework per the Introduction and Section 7, What is the Agency IT Portfolio Summary; Section 11, What is the Major IT Business Case; and Section 13, How do IT Infrastructure, IT Security, and IT Management Standard Investments differ from Major Business Cases, of the OMB, FY 2021 IT Budget – Capital Planning Guidance.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
cross_references: DR 3130-013, Information Technology Capital Planning and Investment Control

Introduction and Section 7, What is the Agency IT Portfolio Summary; Section 11, What is the Major IT Business Case; and Section 13, How do IT Infrastructure, IT Security, and IT Management Standard Investments differ from Major Business Cases, of the OMB, FY 2021 IT Budget – Capital Planning Guidance
policy_statements.target: IT capital planning and investment control (CPIC) practices

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will improve the Authorization to Operate (ATO) process to modernize and adapt the process to the RPA landscape, eliminate duplication of efforts, take advantage of inheritable security controls, and innovate Departmental approaches to security authorization within RPA solutions.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must refer to the Federal Chief Information Officer (CIO) Council guidance, The Application Rationalization Playbook, for best practices to evaluate existing Departmental contracts and RPA solutions for applicability before acquiring or developing new services.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
cross_references: Federal Chief Information Officer (CIO) Council guidance, The Application Rationalization Playbook
policy_statements.target: Federal Chief Information Officer (CIO) Council guidance, The Application Rationalization Playbook
conditions: before acquiring or developing new services

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must notify the RPA CoE for all RPA related acquisitions.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must coordinate with the Office of Contracting and Procurement (OCP), USDA Contracting Desk Book 3.2, to include clear, detailed SLAs and language in acquisition vehicles that protect the interests of USDA and allow for adequate administrative control, security monitoring, reporting, continuous visibility of assets, vendor performance measurements, clearly defined roles and responsibilities, remediation for non-compliance, and risk mitigation.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
cross_references: Office of Contracting and Procurement (OCP), USDA Contracting Desk Book 3.2

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must employ the practice of category management to, where possible, procure common goods and services as a Department to eliminate redundancies, increase efficiency, and deliver more value and savings per OMB, M-19-13, Category Management: Making Smarter Use of Common Contract Solutions and Practices, and DR 3107-001, Management of USDA IT Enterprise Initiatives.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
cross_references: OMB, M-19-13, Category Management: Making Smarter Use of Common Contract Solutions and Practices
DR 3107-001, Management of USDA IT Enterprise Initiatives

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA CIO will:
Serve as the chief policy advisor to the Secretary on RPA policy;
Develop and maintain Departmentwide RPA policy for USDA; and
Ensure the Office of the General Counsel (OGC) is engaged for advice and counsel concerning the acquisition and offering of RPA services, when appropriate.
The Associate Chief Information Officer (ACIO), DISC will:
Serve as Director of the USDA RPA CoE;
Direct the USDA enterprise-class RPA service development;
Implement and execute the necessary internal controls to proactively monitor, measure, audit, report, and enforce compliance with the provisions of the directive;
Establish a Department-level RPA CoE to monitor, guide, and report all RPA activity at USDA;

Design, develop, and implement networking architectures that provide DISC customers with the secure, multi-tenant, Platform as a Service (PaaS) infrastructure to deliver RPA services with 99.9% availability to Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices;
Use the RPA CoE to serve the Department for all day-to-day RPA adoption efforts;
Ensure all new USDA RPA adoption efforts go through the RPA CoE to establish proper awareness and handling of enterprise RPA solutions;
policy_statements.target: all new USDA RPA adoption efforts

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the RPA policy coordinator and technical advisor to the USDA CIO;
policy_statements.resulting_status: RPA policy coordinator and technical advisor

policy_statements.source_text: Administer any certifications regarding RPA services and automation-based information systems that are required;
policy_statements.target: any certifications regarding RPA services and automation-based information systems

policy_statements.source_text: Provide signature authority for routine RPA correspondence to Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices from the OCIO; and
policy_statements.target: routine RPA correspondence to Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices from the OCIO

policy_statements.source_text: Partner with Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices to ensure the effective and efficient use of RPA services.
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), OCIO-ISC, will:
Advise the USDA CIO about strategies and methodologies for securing RPA services;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), OCIO-ISC

policy_statements.source_text: Advise policy exception waiver requestors and reviewers on matters related to cybersecurity; and
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), OCIO-ISC
policy_statements.target: policy exception waiver requestors and reviewers

policy_statements.source_text: Improve the ATO process for RPA per DR 3540-003.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), OCIO-ISC

policy_statements.source_text: The Departmental Chief Privacy Officer (CPO), OCIO-ISC-CPO, will ensure RPA service offerings comply with Federal and Departmental privacy requirements, regulations, and policies, including DR 3515-002, Privacy Policy and Compliance for Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
cross_references: DR 3515-002, Privacy Policy and Compliance for Personally Identifiable Information (PII)

policy_statements.source_text: The ACIO, Information Resource Management Center (IRMC) will:
Ensure RPA service offerings comply with Departmental Enterprise Information Technology Governance (EITG) and CPIC policies;

policy_statements.source_text: The Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors, must submit a waiver request to the ACIO DISC for internal coordination and review on behalf of the USDA CIO if:
A policy requirement cannot be met as explicitly stated; or
Current USDA RPA CoE standards and offerings do not meet the mission needs;

The waiver request must explain the reason for the request, identify compensating controls or actions that meet the policy’s intent, and identify how the compensating controls or actions provide a comparable or greater level of defense or compliance than required by the policy; and

Waivers approved by the USDA CIO must be associated with a National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Special Publication (SP) 800-53 (Rev. 5), Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations, control, recorded, and tracked as a POA&M item in the USDA FISMA data management and reporting tool.
cross_references: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Special Publication (SP) 800-53 (Rev. 5), Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
policy_statements.target: Waivers approved by the USDA CIO

policy_statements.source_text: Waivers will expire at the end of the FY or 6 months from the date of approval, whichever is longer.
conditions: at the end of the FY or 6 months from the date of approval, whichever is longer

policy_statements.source_text: Unless otherwise specified, Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must review and renew approved policy waivers every FY.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

extract_result.purpose:
a. This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for implementing the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Memorandum M-18-23, Shifting From Low-Value to High-Value Work across the USDA. It addresses the establishment of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) through the Center of Excellence (CoE) within the USDA Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO).
b. RPA tools are software programs designed to interact with existing applications and automate routine rules-based tasks by mimicking user interactions. RPA tools reduce the burden of repetitive, simple tasks on employees, and have the potential to save time and taxpayer dollars, improve accuracy and productivity, ensure standardization and consistency of service, and free Federal employees to focus on more meaningful and analytical work.
extract_result.scope: This policy applies to all USDA RPA capable processes and systems in USDA, and to Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, contractors, grantees, and others working for or on behalf of USDA.

b. RPA tools are software programs designed to interact with existing applications and automate routine rules-based tasks by mimicking user interactions. RPA tools reduce the burden of repetitive, simple tasks on employees, and have the potential to save time and taxpayer dollars, improve accuracy and productivity, ensure standardization and consistency of service, and free Federal employees to focus on more meaningful and analytical work.
This policy applies to all USDA RPA capable processes and systems in USDA, and to Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, contractors, grantees, and others working for or on behalf of USDA.
